title: Final Report: [Obesity]
text:
Obesity has emerged as a major public health problem. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported the prevalence rate of obesity in the United States as 40.3% during 2021 - 2023 period [1]. Unlike acute illnesses, the health consequences of obesity typically develop gradually. Obesity accelerates biological aging by promoting chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, all of which contribute to the earlier onset of age-related diseases [2]. It increases the risk of numerous chronic conditions, including type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, hypertension, and certain types of cancers [3, 4]. In this project I want to test the relationship between lifestyle factors and obesity. I expect for example that regular physical activity is associated with lower obesity levels. Hypothesis (H1): Healthier lifestyle habits are associated with lower obesity rates. Null hypothesis (H0): There is no correlation between lifestyle and obesity. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the problem and alter public health strategies.



Obesity Prediction dataset was used in this project. It is available on Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ruchikakumbhar/obesity-prediction
The dataset included 2,111 participants and 17 variables related to demographics, lifestyle, and obesity level.

The results suggest that obesity is influenced by several factors. Participants with higher obesity levels generally had lower physical activity, were more likely to report a family history of obesity, and more frequently consumed high-calorie foods.
Limitation of this study is that the dataset is observational, so it cannot prove cause and effect. In addition, some obesity groups contained very few participants of one gender, making those comparisons less reliable.

title: Final Report: [Obesity]
text: Obesity has emerged as a major public health problem. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported the prevalence rate of obesity in the United States as 40.3% during 2021 - 2023 period [1]. Unlike acute illnesses, the health consequences of obesity typically develop gradually. Obesity accelerates biological aging by promoting chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, all of which contribute to the earlier onset of age-related diseases [2]. It increases the risk of numerous chronic conditions, including type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, hypertension, and certain types of cancers [3, 4]. In this project I want to test the relationship between lifestyle factors and obesity. I expect for example that regular physical activity is associated with lower obesity levels. Hypothesis (H1): Healthier lifestyle habits are associated with lower obesity rates. Null hypothesis (H0): There is no correlation between lifestyle and obesity. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the problem and alter public health strategies.

title: Setup Instructions for Students
text:
Follow these steps to set up and publish your research website.


Before you begin, make sure you have the following:

A GitHub account (free at github.com)
GitHub Desktop installed on your computer
R and RStudio







Click the “Use this template” button.
Select Create a new repository.
Use the Owner dropdown menu to select your github user
Name the repository. This will be in your web address! Choose something professional like your name.
Click Create repository from template.
You should now have this newly created repository on your own GitHub.





On your computer: Make sure the GitHub Desktop is open.
On GitHub: In your own repository on GitHub, Click the “<> Code” button.
Select Open with GitHub Desktop.
Choose a local path for the placement of the directory (not a cloud service). For example: (/Users/YourUserame/GitHub/introR2026)
Select Clone.





[!IMPORTANT] 1. Open RStudio 2. Create a new Rproj file in the existing local directory of your repository 3. Open .Rproj file 4. Edit the following files in RStudio




Replace “Your Name” with your name.
Update the About Me section.
Add your research interests.
Replace “your photo.jpg” with the filename of a photo of yourself & by adding the photo to the directory.
Update places that say “link” with the correct internet link or email address, if desired.





Update the descriptions of your projects.
Add links to additional projects as you create them.





Change the title to your project title.
Write your final report.
Replace all placeholder text with your own content.




styles.css * Customize colors, fonts, and other styling options if desired.
_quarto.yml * add new links to the navbar
README.md * This is a place to add information to the GitHub reponsitory, but will not be displayed on your rendered website.
.gitignore * List files here you don’t want synced to GitHub. For example, if you want to keep your data.csv files local and not online list them here
SETUP.md * These are instructions to create this site. No need to modify this file.




In RStudio, you can preview your website before publishing.
Run the following command in the RStudio Terminal:
quarto preview
To render the website before pushing your changes, run:
quarto render



When you are satisfied with your changes:

Open GitHub Desktop.
Review the files you modified.
Enter a commit summary and an optional description.
Click Commit to main.
Click Push origin to upload your changes to GitHub.





Go to your repository on GitHub.
Click Settings.
Select Pages from the left sidebar.
Under Build and deployment:

Source: Select Deploy from a branch.
Branch: Select main.
Folder: Select /docs.

Click Save.





Wait 1–2 minutes for GitHub to deploy your site.
Return to Settings → Pages.
You should see a URL similar to:
https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/YOUR-REPOSITORY/
Click the link to view your website.





Whenever you want to update your website:

Edit your .qmd files.
Commit and push your changes using GitHub Desktop.
Wait 1–2 minutes for GitHub Pages to rebuild your site.
Refresh your browser to view the updated website.




If your website is not updating:

Go to your GitHub repository.
Click the Actions tab.
Open the most recent workflow run.
Review any error messages if the build failed.







Go to Settings → Pages.
Confirm that:

The branch is set to main.
The folder is set to /docs.

Your website URL should appear on this page after deployment.




Always use forward slashes (/) in links, even when using Windows.
# Correct
[Link](projects/final-report.qmd)

# Incorrect
[Link](projects\final-report.qmd)




To add another page, such as a poster, publication, or additional project:

Create a new .qmd file in the projects/ folder.
Edit projects.qmd and add a link to the new page.
Commit and push your changes.
Wait 1–2 minutes for GitHub Pages to update your website.

text:
Here are my research projects and work:


My final project for CELL 6351 - Intro to Reproducible Data Analysis Using R. Obesity has emerged as a major public health problem. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported the prevalence rate of obesity in the United States as 40.3% during 2021 - 2023 period [1]. Unlike acute illnesses, the health consequences of obesity typically develop gradually. Obesity accelerates biological aging by promoting chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, all of which contribute to the earlier onset of age-related diseases [2]. It increases the risk of numerous chronic conditions, including type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, hypertension, and certain types of cancers [3, 4]. In this project I want to test the relationship between lifestyle factors and obesity. I expect for example that regular physical activity is associated with lower obesity levels. Hypothesis (H1): Healthier lifestyle habits are associated with lower obesity rates. Null hypothesis (H0): There is no correlation between lifestyle and obesity. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the problem and alter public health strategies.
